text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a shared repository. Instead of waiting until the end of a project, developers integrate their work several times a day. Each integration is then verified by an automated build and a series of tests. This process is managed by a CI pipeline, which runs automatically every time new code is pushed. The main goal is to catch issues early, before they become complex and expensive to fix. By running tests frequently, the team receives immediate feedback, allowing them to resolve problems quickly and maintain a stable codebase throughout development.
